title: Nvida stock analysis before its earnings
body: Nvidia stock lost 12.75% while Nasdaq futures gained 3%. Now comes the $167-$174 test Nvidia's sharp rebound from $148.80 was followed by another selloff. With earnings approaching and a new interim CEO in place, the next price tests could reveal whether buyers are regaining confidence or merely interrupting a larger decline. Nvidia shares (NVDA) fell 12.75% in the week ended November 13, while E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures (NQ) gained 3.02%. That is an important divergence for a stock widely regarded as a barometer of the artificial intelligence trade. The message is not that Nvidia must recover or that technology stocks are immune to further selling. It is that Nvidia's weakness has been considerably greater than that of its benchmark, and traders should watch whether that gap starts closing or becomes even more pronounced. For Nvidia bulls, the first meaningful recovery test is approximately $167-$174. For bears, the ability of buyers to defend $158-$162 may be equally important. Nvidia's rebound looked impressive. Friday exposed its weakness. The sequence of Nvidia's recent trading is more informative than the weekly percentage decline alone. On Monday, November 9, the stock opened near $173 following the previous Friday's $186.64 close. It subsequently recovered toward $179, but still finished the session lower. Tuesday brought renewed selling. Wednesday offered another recovery attempt, taking Nvidia to $177.54 before the stock settled at $173.73.

title: ECB's Nagel says another rate hike 'highly probable' as energy prices push inflation
body: An explicit signal from the Bundesbank president that further tightening is likely should support the euro and push up short-dated euro zone yields, especially German two-year debt. Because he ties the risk directly to gas and electricity, euro zone rate pricing is now more sensitive to moves in energy markets, so a rise in oil or gas could feed quickly into ECB hike expectations. His comment that the economy has proved resilient also weakens the argument that growth worries will hold the ECB back, which leaves rate-sensitive European equities more exposed. --- Not only open mouths at the ECB: Weekend Fed speak: Collins backs steady, gradual rate hikes, cool on a bigger December move Sunday Fed talk: Schmid says inflation would still be near 3% without energy, Fed has work to do ---- Nagel has made it clear that the ECB is not finished: with energy prices running ahead of forecasts and expectations creeping higher, Germany's central bank chief sees another hike as the likely price of avoiding a 2022 rerun. Summary: Joachim Nagel, ECB Governing Council member and Bundesbank president, said it is highly probable the ECB will have to raise rates again if conditions do not change. He warned that every month of elevated inflation raises the risk of second-round effects. Energy prices have moved well above the path in the September projections, pushing the outlook toward the adverse scenario.

title: New Zealand services PSI hits 3.5-year high at 51.7, fifth straight month of growth
body: A services reading at a multi-year high, led by new orders, strengthens the case that New Zealand's recovery is spreading beyond a handful of sectors. That gives the New Zealand dollar modest support on the domestic data front. For rate expectations, firmer activity reduces the pressure for further policy support. The flat employment reading and persistent cost-of-living complaints, however, point to slack that has not yet closed. Traders are likely to treat the data as a confidence builder rather than a game changer, and will look to the next few releases to see whether spending held back during the election starts to come through. --- Also: NZ manufacturing PMI eases to 54.9 in October but extends expansion run to 16 months --- New Zealand's services firms are finally seeing new business arrive in volume heading into summer, but with hiring still flat, October's strength looks more like a pre-Christmas lift than a recovery that has fully taken hold. Summary: New Zealand's services PSI rose to 51.7 in October from 50.9, the highest reading in more than three and a half years. It is the fifth consecutive month above the 50 breakeven level. New orders (53.0), activity and sales (52.6) and supplier deliveries (52.1) led the gains. Employment dipped to 49.9, the only sub-index in contraction, and inventories eased to 50.1. The share of negative survey comments fell to 57.9% from 59.9%. Fuel prices, cost of living, interest rates and the election were still the main concerns.

title: Weekend Fed speak: Collins backs steady, gradual rate hikes, cool on a bigger December move
body: Collins's comments push back on the half-point talk that has built since Waller's remarks and last week's inflation data. That could trim some of the tail pricing for a larger December move and take a little heat out of the front end of the Treasury curve. Her view that the eventual rate path may be higher cuts the other way, though. It supports the idea of a longer hiking cycle, which keeps the US dollar supported on dips and leaves gold without a clear dovish tailwind. For traders, her message is about the pace of hikes, not when they stop. --- Also: Sunday Fed talk: Schmid says inflation would still be near 3% without energy, Fed has work to do --- Collins wants the Fed to keep hiking in small steps rather than speed up, but her admission that the destination may be higher means a gentler pace should not be confused with a softer stance. Summary: Boston Fed President Susan Collins favours continuing to raise rates at a steady, modest pace, while remaining open-minded. She sees two-sided risks: inflation is high and broadening, the job market is stable and could accelerate, and further shocks remain possible. Higher medium and longer-term rates since the start of the year may weigh on demand more than she expects. She argued against shifting to a more aggressive pace of hikes, and said gradual does not mean a fixed cadence. Recent price data and a firmer labour market suggest the policy rate path over the next year may be higher than she thought.

title: Sunday Fed talk: Schmid says inflation would still be near 3% without energy, Fed has work to do
body: Schmid's remarks add weight to hike pricing that is already in place for December. His attack on the "supply shock" argument also makes it harder to make the dovish case for looking through energy-driven inflation. That supports the US dollar and front-end Treasury yields, and it keeps the small tail risk of a half-point move alive. A Fed seen as committed to further tightening has been a headwind for gold throughout this cycle. His view that AI-driven demand will respond to higher rates is also a reminder to rate-sensitive tech valuations that the sector is not exempt from policy. --- Schmid stopped short of calling for a hike, but he took apart both main arguments that inflation is beyond the Fed's control, leaving little room for the doves ahead of December. Summary: Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said inflation is running too hot, uncomfortably above the 2% target and moving in the wrong direction. He said inflation would still be around 3% with energy prices excluded. He rejected views that supply shocks, or AI-driven demand that is resistant to rates, put inflation beyond the Fed's reach. He said the labour market is broadly in balance, with little evidence that wages are adding to inflation. He did not specifically call for more hikes. Markets are fully priced for a quarter-point rise in December. Schmid is not a voting member of the FOMC this year.

title: Jensen Huang weighs Nvidia comeback days after quitting over scandal, FT reports
body: The comeback talk adds a new layer of uncertainty to Nvidia shares going into Tuesday's results, and traders now have two outcomes to price: an outside successor or a return of the founder. A Huang return could ease worries about execution during the product ramp, but it would bring back regulatory and China-export risk while US inquiries are still open. Because Nvidia's weighting is so large, any swing in its shares on the leadership news is likely to spill into the wider AI and semiconductor complex, including Asian chip suppliers. Newswire cut: Jensen Huang is weighing a return as Nvidia CEO days after resigning over a scandal, the FT reported, as allies build a Silicon Valley 'war room' to lobby the board and the White House. Nvidia reports results on Tuesday under an interim chief. One-line wrap: Days after quitting over a scandal with national security overtones, Jensen Huang is weighing a return, setting allies with White House ambitions against a board that has already approached Arm's CEO about the job. Summary: Jensen Huang has discussed a possible return as Nvidia CEO with people close to him, days after resigning. An ally is organising a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby the board and seek White House support, and Huang backs the effort. Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, one with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China. Nvidia's board had already approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor.

title: Economic and event calendar in Asia, Monday, November 16, 2026. BoJ, China data, Japan GDP.
body: Busy session coming up: 1. Japan Q3 GDP, preliminary (23:50 GMT / 6:50 pm ET Sunday) Consensus: +0.1% q/q and +0.3% annualised, down from +0.4% q/q and +1.4% annualised in Q2. The deflator is expected to hold at 2.6% y/y. Preview: In a poll of 16 economists, the median estimate is 0.3% annualised growth for July to September, with weaker consumption and external demand outweighing a recovery in capital spending. Private consumption makes up more than half of Japan's GDP, so a decline there pulls hard on the headline. Daiwa is more upbeat than the consensus. It forecasts +1.5% annualised (+0.4% q/q), which would be a fourth straight quarter of growth. It sees a small fall in private consumption, with capex and exports lifting the total. It also expects capex to bounce back from one-off factors that weighed on it in Q2. Why it matters: The release lands about a month before the BoJ's December meeting. The next policy meeting is 17–18 December, and a Reuters poll has the BoJ hiking to 1.50% then, keeping to a quarterly pace. A soft print with a weak consumption breakdown would give the doves some material. A solid capex number would help the hawks. 2. China October activity data (02:00 GMT / 9:00 pm ET Sunday) Consensus: Retail sales +0.8% y/y (prior 1.1%). Industrial production +5.3% y/y (prior 5.5%). Fixed asset investment year-to-date -7.0% (prior -7.2%). Background: September came in firmer than expected.
